name: Bergdoktorhaus Köpfinghof Going
kurzbeschreibung: The Bergdoktorhaus Köpfinghof in Going am Wilden Kaiser: original filming location of the hit ZDF TV series featuring a traditional parlour, herb garden, and Kaiser view.
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Bergdoktorhaus Köpfinghof is situated on a sunny high plateau in the hamlet of Sonnseite above the municipality of Going am Wilden Kaiser (Kitzbühel district) at an elevation of around 850 metres. This over 300-year-old, heritage-protected Tyrolean farmstead achieved cult status across Europe as the primary original filming location of the popular television series "Der Bergdoktor" (ZDF and ORF). As a flourishing excursion destination, the farm attracts tens of thousands of series fans, hikers, and cultural travelers every year, all eager to see the authentic film set close up against the unobstructed dream backdrop of the Wilder Kaiser massif.

Film History, Living Culture & Wilder Kaiser

Ever since filming commenced in 2007, the historic Köpfinghof has portrayed the fictional farmstead of the Gruber family, featuring the famous parlour of Dr. Martin Gruber (played by Hans Sigl), his mother Lisbeth, and his daughter Lilli. During a tour through the meticulously preserved timber blockhouse, visitors explore the authentic film sets: highlights include the cosy wood-panelled Gruber-Wohnstube with its tiled masonry stove, the rustic farmhouse kitchen, the traditional Herrgottswinkel (devotional corner), and the famous wooden panoramic balcony terrace where countless emotional key scenes were filmed. Informational display boards and photo walls document fascinating behind-the-scenes insights into the TV production, actor anecdotes, and the logistical challenges of film shoots in alpine terrain. Fronting the house, a lovingly tended cottage garden with historic medicinal herbs invites visitors to linger. The forecourt by the barn gate provides one of the most photographed panoramic vistas in Tyrol, framing the jagged limestone peaks of Ellmauer Halt, Treffauer, and Scheffauer.

Visit & Getting There

The Bergdoktorhaus Köpfinghof is open for public visits during the summer months from mid-May to mid-October on designated weekdays: Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 09:30 to 12:00 (the house may remain closed on filming days at short notice; current shooting schedules and opening hours are updated weekly on the tourism association's website). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €4.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €2.00, small children free. Holders of the regional Wilder Kaiser GästeCard receive discounted admission. Getting there by car: via the B178 (Loferer Straße) to Going am Wilden Kaiser; due to narrow alpine lanes, private vehicular traffic is prohibited at the farmstead itself. Park at the large hikers' car park Going Dorf or the Pramerburg car park (parking fees apply). From there, a delightful, approximately 25-minute walk (around 1.5 km) leads gently uphill to the Köpfinghof. By public transport: ÖBB train to St. Johann in Tirol railway station, then take bus route 4060 to Going (stop Going Stanglwirt or Going Dorf); in summer, the free KaiserJet hiking shuttle also operates.

Tips

The footpath up to the Köpfinghof is paved or fine gravel and easily manageable with prams; access into the farmhouse involves just a few steps. Combine your visit with a detour to the picturesque village square in Going, where the historic Gasthof "Wilder Kaiser" and the village fountain serve as additional well-known filming locations from the series.
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Mai bis Mitte Okt Di, Mi, Fr, Sa 09:30–12:00 Uhr (außer an Drehtagen)
